Note::is_alnum¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::is_alnum() const

Test Whether Every Character In A Cell Is A Letter Or Digit¶

is_alnum() reports, for each cell, whether the cell is non-empty and every byte is an ASCII letter or digit (A–Z, a–z, 0–9). Use it to validate identifier-like fields — slugs, codes, keys — that must contain no spaces, punctuation, or separators.

The check is ASCII-only (byte-level), so é, ü, or any non-Latin letter fails the cell. An empty cell is 0, consistent with the rest of the is_* family.

Return value¶

A Bool Note with the receiver’s shape, one native truth value per cell. Use bools() for a borrowed contiguous host view.

Example 1: A Batch¶

const auto n = pluss::make_note(
    {"abc", "abc123", "123", "abc_123", "", "a b"});
const auto mask = n.is_alnum();
std::cout << "[";
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < mask.bools().size(); ++i)
  std::cout << (i ? ", " : "") << static_cast<int>(mask.bools()[i]);
std::cout << "]\n";

Output¶

[1, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0]

"abc_123" has an underscore, the empty cell has nothing, and "a b" has a space — all 0.

See Also¶

  • Note::is_alpha / Note::is_digit: the narrower checks.

  • Note::contains_any_digit / Note::contains_any_alpha: “has at least one” rather than “is all”.
